books.title: Everything, Everything
books.author: Nicola Yoon
books.description: A high-concept, emotionally intimate romance about a girl confined to her home due to a rare illness and the boy who challenges everything she believes about safety, love, and risk. Told through vignettes, drawings, and diary entries, the novel explores control, fear, and what it means to truly live.
books.review: Widely praised for its inventive format and emotional punch. Readers love its tenderness and accessibility, though some feel the ending resolves too quickly.

books.title: Parachutes
books.author: Kelly Yang
books.description: A dual-perspective novel examining power, privilege, and trauma through the intersecting lives of two teens navigating wealth, immigration, and abuse at an elite California high school.
books.review: Often described as challenging but essential. Readers praise its honesty and layered characters, while noting the themes are heavy and emotionally demanding.

books.title: Catalog of Burnt Objects
books.author: Shana Youngdahl
books.description: Set against the backdrop of devastating California wildfires, this lyrical novel explores grief, first love, and fractured families as a teen searches for stability amid literal and emotional destruction.
books.review: Highly praised for its prose and atmosphere. Readers call it haunting and immersive, though it is a slower, more reflective read.

books.title: Love Is a Revolution
books.author: Renée Watson
books.description: A Harlem-set coming-of-age story about a teen who performs activism for love before being forced to confront what real identity, community, and accountability actually mean.
books.review: Celebrated for its voice and cultural specificity. Readers appreciate its critique of performative activism and its thoughtful emotional arc.

books.title: Ballad of Darcy and Russell
books.author: Morgan Matson
books.description: A one-night romance that unfolds during a liminal moment between high school and adulthood, capturing fleeting intimacy, possibility, and the ache of inevitable goodbyes.
books.review: Fans love its nostalgic tone and emotional softness. Some note it follows familiar Matson patterns but still delivers.

books.title: Henry Hamlet’s Heart
books.author: Rhiannon Wilde
books.description: A queer best-friends-to-lovers rom-com centered on awkwardness, emotional honesty, and the fear of risking a friendship for love.
books.review: Praised for authenticity and humor. Readers relate strongly to the emotional vulnerability, though some moments are intentionally cringe.

books.title: Lucky in Love
books.author: Kasie West
books.description: A feel-good romantic comedy about sudden wealth, social pressure, and discovering who genuinely cares when everything changes overnight.
books.review: A comfort read beloved for its charm and pacing. Predictable but satisfying.

books.title: Love, Life, and the List
books.author: Kasie West
books.description: A creative self-challenge turns into an emotional journey as a teen artist confronts fear, love, and what it really means to grow.
books.review: Readers enjoy the structure and emotional clarity, though stakes remain relatively low.

books.title: As You Walk On By
books.author: Julian Winters
books.description: An ensemble-driven prom-night novel where multiple teens confront identity, friendship, and expectation during one chaotic evening.
books.review: Strongly praised for voice and pacing. Some readers note the large cast can be hard to track.

books.title: Right Where I Left You
books.author: Julian Winters
books.description: A geek-culture-infused queer romance about friendship, anxiety, and miscommunication during a pivotal summer before college.
books.review: A fan favorite for its warmth and relatability, with minor critiques about plot convenience.

books.title: Bingsu for Two
books.author: Sujin Witherspoon
books.description: A cozy yet emotionally grounded fake-dating romance set in a struggling Korean café, blending food, grief, and self-discovery.
books.review: Readers love the atmosphere and emotional beats, though some side characters feel underdeveloped.

books.title: Nothing Burns as Bright as You
books.author: Ashley Woodfolk
books.description: A nonlinear exploration of queer love, grief, and emotional dependency told through fragmented timelines and intense introspection.
books.review: Praised for poetic writing but divisive due to its structure and emotional heaviness.

books.title: Louder Than Words
books.author: Ashley Woodfolk
books.description: A podcast-driven mystery examining secrecy, reputation, and trauma as a teen’s past threatens to resurface publicly.
books.review: Engaging premise with relevant themes, though some readers wanted deeper resolution.

books.title: Harbor Me
books.author: Jacqueline Woodson
books.description: A quiet, discussion-based novel where a group of middle-school students find healing by sharing their fears in a safe space.
books.review: Highly respected for emotional honesty, though often categorized closer to middle grade.

books.title: Instructions for Dancing
books.author: Nicola Yoon
books.description: A magical realism romance where a girl can see how relationships will end, forcing her to reconsider love after heartbreak.
books.review: Sweet and readable, though more predictable than the author’s debut.

books.title: The Donut Prince of New York
books.author: Allen Zadoff
books.description: A heartfelt coming-of-age story about body image, ambition, and belonging as a plus-size teen playwright is unexpectedly recruited onto his high school football team.
books.review: Readers praise its warmth, humor, and nuanced look at masculinity.

books.title: Quiver
books.author: Julia Watts
books.description: Set in rural Tennessee, this novel explores an unlikely friendship across political and cultural divides.
books.review: Frequently praised for its courage and nuance.

books.title: I Like Me Better
books.author: Robby Weber
books.description: A summery queer romance set at a seaside conservation center.
books.review: Sweet, affirming, and light.

books.title: The Art of Insanity
books.author: Christine Webb
books.description: A teen artist hides her bipolar diagnosis while navigating love and pressure.
books.review: Praised for authenticity and emotional vulnerability.

books.title: Diary of a Confused Feminist
books.author: Kate Weston
books.description: A humorous diary-style exploration of modern feminism and anxiety.
books.review: Funny and relatable, with intentional cringe.

books.title: The Grove
books.author: Brooks Whitney Phillips
books.description: A haunting historical coming-of-age novel set in 1960s Florida.
books.review: Atmospheric and emotionally intense.

books.title: Last Chance Dance
books.author: Lakita Wilson
books.description: A joyful senior-year romance built around one final dance tradition.
books.review: Praised for humor and heart.

books.title: Seven Minutes in Candyland
books.author: Brian Wasson
books.description: A witty rom-com about emotional labor and first love.
books.review: Original and funny.

books.title: If You, Then Me
books.author: Yvonne Woon
books.description: A tech-forward rom-com exploring AI and identity.
books.review: Interesting premise with mixed pacing.

books.title: Mysterious Ways
books.author: Wendy Wunder
books.description: A darkly funny novel about secrets and mental health.
books.review: Conceptually strong but polarizing.

books.title: Be More Chill
books.author: Ned Vizzini
books.description: A cult-classic YA satire about popularity and insecurity.
books.review: Beloved for its humor and musical adaptation.

books.title: This Side of Home
books.author: Renée Watson
books.description: A thoughtful exploration of gentrification and sisterhood.
books.review: Respected for emotional maturity.
